title: Workload Courier: synthesizer for continuous batching policies and safe-apply
creator: Elliot Chen
description: Design and implement the Workload Courier: a synthesizer that turns continuous workload profiles into safe, versioned batching & cache policies. Goals: (1) convert sampled per-tenant/per-route traffic signatures into compact policy candidates, (2) score candidates by cost/latency/regression risk heuristics, (3) run staged, automated safe-apply with shadow evaluation and rollback hooks. This ticket covers algorithm design, telemetry hooks, rollout orchestration surface, and initial ETA/rollback rules.
background: We have a gap between rich profiling telemetry and safe automated config application. SRE and customers request an automated system that reduces per-token cost while avoiding QoE regressions. Existing profiling pipelines emit heatmaps and microburst stats but there is no single synthesizer to propose cohesive batching and KV cache windowing profiles per workload slice. Current manual workflows are time-consuming and error-prone.
deliverables: policy synthesizer service: sample -> candidate generator -> scorer
telemetry enrichment: per-request KV hit/miss, effective batch sizes, latency/COST deltas
safe-apply pipeline: shadow-apply -> canary -> incremental percent rollout -> automated rollback
e2e test harness and CI jobs for gradual rollout simulation
dashboard surface in Console for proposed policy diffs and audit logs
acceptance_criteria: Service generates at least 3 unique policy candidates per workload slice with deterministic seed
Scorer returns a ranked list using cost, p99 latency, and regression risk score
Shadow-apply mode collects telemetry for 100k requests without affecting production outputs
Canary rollout mechanism supports incremental weights (0-100%) and auto-rollback on regressions defined by threshold
Policies are versioned and recorded in audit logs; rollbacks create explicit revert versions
technical_notes: Candidate generator will synthesize parameters: target_batch_window_ms, max_microbatch_size, kv_prefetch_window, kv_eviction_threshold, and dynamic_throttle_bounds. Scoring heuristic is a weighted composite: cost_savings_estimate (token-opportunity-model), p99_delta_penalty, kv_hit_delta_reward, and safety_margin (derived from baseline variability). Use streaming aggregation to keep memory bounded; store candidate fingerprints in Redis for quick lookup. Shadow-apply uses deterministic sampling to route a mirrored request through the policy chain without committing outputs.
design_decisions: 1) Keep candidate space compact via quantized buckets for window sizes to avoid combinatorial explosion. 2) Penalize any candidate with >3% increase in p99 over 10k-sample windows unless cost savings > 25%. 3) Use conservative default rollout increments (5% steps) with 30m observation windows and early rollback if error-rate or p99 regression exceeds thresholds. 4) Persist decisions and telemetry slice ids to allow post-mortem replay.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overzealous cost tuning increases tail latency — Mitigation: strict p99 gating and human-in-the-loop holdout for high-risk customers
Risk: Fingerprint collisions produce wrong policy mapping — Mitigation: combine multiple signature dimensions (route, model, seq_len_quartile, customer_id_hash) and include collision metrics
Risk: Telemetry skew during traffic spikes — Mitigation: weight samples by recent traffic volume and require stable window before full apply
implementation_plan: Week 1: prototype candidate generator and scoring microservice; ingest existing profiling streams
Week 2: implement shadow-apply plumbing + telemetry collectors; run closed-loop sims against stored traces
Week 3: integrate canary rollout controller and audit logging; add API endpoints for Console
Week 4: run internal dogfood on non-critical tenants; gather regression metrics and iterate on heuristics
Week 5: documentation, runbook, and launch limited beta with select customers
metrics: Number of automated rollbacks and root causes
